content: 1. A randomized trial was conducted to investigate the relationship between enteritis and malnutrition, as published in the Journal of Paediatrics and Child Health in 2002 (Volume 38, Issue 6, Pages 571–577). 2. Vasquez-Garibay E and colleagues demonstrated that nutritional support with nucleotide supplementation enhances immune response in severely malnourished infants, as reported in the Archives of Medical Research in 2004 (Volume 35, Issue 4, Pages 284–288). 3. Hossain MM and collaborators compared the effectiveness of a locally adapted protocol versus the WHO protocol for hospital management of severely malnourished children, as detailed in Indian Pediatrics in 2009 (Volume 46, Issue 3, Pages 213–217). 4. Oberlin O and Wilkinson C evaluated the relactation process using the supplemental suckling technique, as referenced in their study. 5. Corbett M discussed infant feeding practices within therapeutic feeding programs (TFPs), providing insights into their implementation. 6. Lanese MG highlighted the utility of cup feeding as a valuable tool in neonatal care, as published in the Journal of Human Lactation in 2011 (Volume 27, Issue 1, Pages 12–13). 7. Kumar A, Dabas P, and Singh B found that spoon feeding facilitates earlier hospital discharge for low-birth-weight infants, as reported in the Journal of Perinatology in 2010 (Volume 30, Issue 3, Pages 209–217). 8. Abouelfettoh AM and colleagues conducted a quasi-experimental study comparing cup feeding and bottle feeding in hospitalized late preterm infants in Egypt, as published in the International Breastfeeding Journal in 2008 (Volume 3, Article 27). 9. Flint A, New K, and Davies MW reviewed the efficacy of cup feeding versus other supplemental enteral feeding methods for newborns unable to fully breastfeed, as summarized in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2007 (Issue 2, Article CD005092). 10. Howard CR and colleagues conducted a randomized clinical trial to assess the effects of pacifier use, bottle feeding, and cup feeding on breastfeeding outcomes, as published in Pediatrics in 2003 (Volume 111, Issue 3, Pages 511–518). 11. Collins S and colleagues identified key factors influencing the success of community-based management of severe malnutrition, as detailed in the Food and Nutrition Bulletin in 2006 (Volume 27, Supplement 3, Pages S49–S82). 12. Binns C, James J, and Lee MK raised concerns about the potential negative impact of the new WHO growth charts on breastfeeding, as discussed in the Breastfeeding Review in 2008 (Volume 16, Issue 3, Pages 5–7). 13. Ahmad UA and colleagues analyzed the implications of the new WHO growth standards on infant growth interpretation in Malawi, as presented at the Royal College of Paediatrics & Child Health Spring Meeting in 2011. 14. Fergusson P, Tomkins A, and Kerac M explored strategies to improve the management of severe acute malnutrition in HIV-prevalent settings, as published in International Health in 2009 (Volume 1, Issue 1, Pages 10–16). 15. Kuehl J provided an overview of cup feeding for newborns, emphasizing its practical applications, as published in the Journal of Perinatal & Neonatal Nursing in 1997 (Volume 11, Issue 2, Pages 56–60). 16. Stewart RC reviewed recent evidence on the relationship between maternal depression and infant growth, as published in Maternal & Child Nutrition in 2007 (Volume 3, Issue 2, Pages 94–107). 17. Bizouerne C examined the psychological challenges and insufficient maternal milk supply in Afghanistan, as part of a clinical psychological approach in humanitarian settings, presented at Université Victor Ségalen in 2008. 18. Falbo AR and Alves JG described the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of children hospitalized with severe malnutrition at the Instituto Materno Infantil de Pernambuco (IMIP) in Brazil, as published in Cadernos de Saúde Pública in 2002 (Volume 18, Issue 5, Pages 1473–1477). 19. Kerac M and colleagues analyzed the prevalence of wasting among infants under six months in developing countries and the implications of new case definitions using WHO growth standards, as published in the Archives of Disease in Childhood in 2011 (Volume 96, Issue 11, Pages 1008–1013). 20. Collins S and Yates R emphasized the need to update the classification of acute malnutrition, as discussed in The Lancet in 2003 (Volume 362, Issue 9379, Page 249). 21. Sadler K and colleagues compared the program coverage of two therapeutic feeding interventions implemented in neighboring districts of Malawi, as published in Public Health Nutrition in 2007 (Volume 10, Issue 9, Pages 907–913). 22. Caballero B discussed the long-term risks of adult diseases associated with early nutrition, as published in Public Health Nutrition in 2001 (Volume 4, Issue 6A, Pages 1335–1336). 23. Shrimpton R and colleagues examined the global timing of growth faltering and its implications for nutritional interventions, as published in Pediatrics in 2001 (Volume 107, Issue 5, Article E75).
